title: review: G0: scout and triage worktrees base on the goal branch, not origin/main (Phase G scouts T-0262/T-0263 read code from PR 5 and reported stale findings)
spec: spawn.base_for (spawn.py about line 30) bases execute tasks with a parent on goal/<parent> when that branch exists, reviews on the reviewed task's branch, challenges on the goal branch, and everything else on origin/main. Scout tasks fall into the last bucket: wt/T-0261, wt/T-0262 and wt/T-0263 were cut from 2ae174e (the PR 5 merge on main), so two of three Phase G scouts reported findings about code that no longer exists on goal/T-0260 (no security_paths, no compact bus_read, no fix_round_for). Change: scout and triage tasks with a parent whose goal/<parent> branch exists base on it, falling back to origin/main as today; the scout prompt (scout.md) states the base sha and branch on its first line so a scout can say which code it read. Tests in tests/test_spawn.py: test_scout_bases_on_goal_branch, test_scout_without_goal_branch_uses_origin_main, test_scout_prompt_names_base.
acceptance: Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: base_for() role tuple now also includes "triage" (untested), changing which base branch triage worktrees are cut from. Traced as consistent with existing behavior (triage already shared the scout prompt/else-branch path and already called base_for() via ensure_worktree()), so low risk, but not covered by the acceptance criteria or a dedicated test.
